the combination of a radical leaving group and a stabilizing two-center three-electron interaction in the radical fragment allows for the formation of aromatics in a self-terminating cascade.

the development of new methods for the synthesis of complex molecules.
the development of radical cascades as a new tool in synthetic organic chemistry.
the synthesis and reactivity of radicals.

the combination of aromaticity, half-bonds, and through-bond interactions can be utilized for the design of leaving groups in self-terminaing radical cascades.
the design of leaving groups is a key factor in the success of radical cascades, and that this is particularly true for the β-scission of C C bonds.

we have developed a new concept for the stereoelectronic control of radical reactions.

the combination of a radical leaving group and the presence of an aromatic product allows for β-scission of C C bonds, and that this reactivity can be further enhanced by a through-bond interaction between the radical and the lone pair of the leaving group.

the design of leaving groups can be used as a powerful tool to steer reaction pathways.
